hooks.command: echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"PLAN TRACKING (project rule): if this prompt starts or continues work that runs an ExecForge role (c-level, execforge, eng-level, q-level, sec-level, design-html, full-cycle, CEO/COO review), keep a plan file under plans/. NEW task: create plans/YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS-ss_<title>.md (ss = hundredths of a second; use dashes, never colons — a colon in a committed filename breaks git clone on Windows) using plans/TEMPLATE.md and write the plan BEFORE doing the work. SAME task as an earlier prompt: update that existing file (progress, decisions, status) instead of creating a new one; do not start a second file for the same task. No role involved: no plan file needed. EVERY PLAN FILE CARRIES A '## Risks' SECTION: one block per risk, named Risk A, Risk B, ... Each answers nine questions - how bad (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW); what actually happens (the real impact, who is hurt and how, not the label); short or long term; the solution (or 'none yet'); what the solution would fix (operational load / manual work / automation / compliance, or 'none of these'); the risk of the solution itself ('none' is almost always wrong); cost including ongoing upkeep; what we expect to be true after; and whether a human needs training (if yes, say who must learn what). Never invent a cost or number - write 'not measured'. If there is genuinely no risk, write 'No risks identified' and say why. Shape lives in plans/TEMPLATE.md. RISK ANALYSIS ON EVERY FIX: whenever a bug or failure is fixed, the report on that fix must include a short risk analysis with four parts — (1) BLAST RADIUS: what else this change can affect; (2) NOT FIXED: what the fix leaves unsolved, and any related case it does not cover; (3) DETECTION: what would catch it if it regresses, naming the specific test, gate, or job, or stating plainly that nothing would; (4) ROLLBACK: how to undo it. Keep each to one or two sentences. State the root cause as proven evidence or say it is a hypothesis. WRITE THE PLAN FILE IN PLAIN, SIMPLE ENGLISH: short everyday words, short sentences, no jargon. If a technical term is unavoidable, say in a few words what it means. A reader who does not know this codebase should still follow it."}}'
